chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And give its due on the day of its reaping, and do not be extravagant; surely He does not love the extravagant.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'So-and-so, the Ansari (he mentioned his name), had a farm. When he harvested it, he would give it all in charity, leaving himself and his dependents with nothing. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made that extravagance.'
ai.seo_question: What is considered extravagance in giving charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that 'extravagance' (israf) in the context of charity includes self-neglect, as illustrated by the Ansari companion who gave away his entire harvest, leaving his family destitute. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balance (wasatiyyah), where fulfilling one's primary financial duty to dependents is prioritized over excessive voluntary giving that leads to poverty.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Musna who said,

‘A man asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [6:141] and give the due of it on the day of its reaping, and do not act extravagantly; surely He does not Love the extravagant.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So and so, son of so and so the Helper (he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned his name), had a farm for him, and when he took (the harvest), he gave in charity (all of) it, and there remained himself and his dependants without anything. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made that to be an extravagance’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Muthanna who has said the following:

“A man once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Give His right on the day of its harvest and do not spend excessively; He does not love excessive spenders.’ [6:141]

He (the Imam) said, ‘So and so, he mentioned his name, Ansariy (people of al-Madinah) had a farm. After harvest, he would give all of it in charity. He and his dependents would remain without anything. Thus, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, called such spending excessive.’”
